meta.prompt: You are a worldclass math professor with expertise in breaking down math problems into easy to understand, coherent step

steps.title: Understand the Setup
steps.description:
We have a right triangle with the $90°$ angle sitting at vertex $Q$. That makes $PQ$ and $QR$ the two **legs**, and $PR$ (the side opposite the right angle) the **hypotenuse**.

The Pythagorean theorem says: in any right triangle, $\text{leg}^2 + \text{leg}^2 = \text{hypotenuse}^2$. Since we know both legs, we can find the hypotenuse directly — no rearranging needed.

steps.title: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem
steps.description:
Plug the two legs into $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$:
$$PR^2 = PQ^2 + QR^2 = 30^2 + 40^2 = 900 + 1600 = 2500$$

Recognizing $2500 = 50^2$ gives us $PR = 50$ immediately. Notice $30$-$40$-$50$ is just a scaled-up **3-4-5 Pythagorean triple** (multiply every side by $10$), so the answer is a clean whole number.

steps.title: Find sin(∠QPR)
steps.description:
For angle $\angle QPR$ (the angle at vertex $P$), SOH-CAH-TOA tells us:
$$\sin(\angle QPR) = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$$

The side **opposite** $\angle QPR$ is $QR = 40$, and the **hypotenuse** is $PR = 50$:
$$\sin(\angle QPR) = \frac{40}{50} = \frac{4}{5}$$
